reports.title: Complete Blood Count (CBC) Diagnostic Analysis
reports.summary: The document is a printed Complete Blood Count (CBC) lab report for a 29-year-old male patient, Mr. Ketan Chavan. While hemoglobin (15 g%), PCV (36%), and total WBC counts (5,500/cu.mm) are within normal reference ranges, the report demonstrates a critical, severe elevation in platelet count at 1,550,000/cu.mm (Severe Thrombocytosis). Additionally, RBC indices indicate microcytosis with a low MCV (72.00 fL) and an elevated MCHC (41.67%). Urgent medical evaluation by a hematologist is required due to the risks associated with extreme thrombocytosis.

parameters.interpretation: Hemoglobin concentration is within healthy limits for adult males.
Red blood cell count is within normal physiological limits.
Hematocrit level is within normal range.
Indicates microcytosis (smaller than average red blood cell size).
Average amount of hemoglobin per RBC is within normal limits.
Elevated hemoglobin concentration relative to cell volume.
Variation in red blood cell size is normal.
Overall white blood cell count is normal, indicating no active leukocytosis.
Neutrophil percentage is within normal limits.
Lymphocyte percentage is within normal limits.
Eosinophil count is normal.
Monocyte percentage is normal.
Basophil count is normal.
Severe thrombocytosis (>1.5 million/cu.mm), requiring urgent hematological evaluation.

findings: Profound, severe thrombocytosis with a platelet count of 1,550,000 /cu.mm (Normal upper limit: 450,000 /cu.mm).
Microcytosis indicated by a decreased MCV of 72.00 fl (Normal: 80 - 99 fl).
Elevated MCHC of 41.67% (Normal: 30 - 34%).
Normal total leukocyte count (5,500 /cu.mm) and differential leukocyte distribution.
Normal Hemoglobin (15 g%) and PCV (36%).
recommendations: Seek urgent evaluation with a Hematologist for diagnostic workup of extreme thrombocytosis.
Order iron studies (Serum Ferritin, Serum Iron, Total Iron Binding Capacity) to rule out iron-deficiency reactive thrombocytosis.
Perform genetic testing (e.g., JAK2 V617F mutation screening) to evaluate potential myeloproliferative neoplasms if reactive causes are excluded.
Repeat CBC with a manual peripheral blood smear review to confirm true platelet elevation and rule out platelet clumping.
Monitor closely for symptoms such as headache, visual changes, chest pain, leg swelling, or unusual bruising/bleeding.
